title: RAG: give your AI the right context
description: Connect a language model to knowledge it can actually reference.
objectives: Diagnose retrieval separately from answer quality
explanation: Retrieval-augmented generation supplies relevant source material to a model at request time. An ingestion pipeline extracts text, separates it into searchable pieces, and stores those pieces with metadata. At query time, a retriever selects candidates and the application supplies useful evidence to the generator.

Retrieval quality sets a ceiling on grounded answers. If the correct passage is missing, a carefully written prompt cannot recover it from your private documents. Evaluate whether retrieval finds the required evidence before evaluating whether the generated answer uses it correctly.

Preserve source titles, locations, dates, and access rules through the pipeline. An answer needs a traceable citation, and retrieval must not expose documents the user cannot access. RAG helps with changing knowledge, but it does not make every answer correct or every document trustworthy.

terms.definition: A searchable portion of a source document.
A component that selects candidate evidence.
A component that reorders retrieved candidates for relevance.

example: For a benefits assistant, ingest approved policy sections with title, date, and department permissions. Retrieve passages for a question, check access, and ask the model to answer using those passages with citations. If support is absent, return a clear knowledge gap.
mistakes: Scoring only the final answer and ignoring missing evidence.
Assuming every retrieved passage is authoritative.
exercise: Create a five-document mini knowledge base. Write ten questions and identify the exact supporting paragraph for each before testing retrieval.

questions.question: Does RAG usually update model weights?
questions.answer: No. It normally retrieves external information into request context; changing weights is a separate training process.
questions.distractor: Yes, retrieval trains the model on every document.

questions.question: What metadata should survive ingestion?
questions.answer: Source identity, location, freshness, and access controls should remain available for citations, updates, and authorization.
questions.distractor: Only the raw text; metadata has no use.

questions.question: The answer is wrong because the right paragraph was not retrieved. What should you fix first?
questions.answer: Inspect ingestion, query handling, and retrieval recall before changing the generation prompt.

questions.question: Why evaluate retrieval separately?
questions.answer: It distinguishes evidence-selection failures from generation failures, making improvements more targeted and measurable.
questions.distractor: It proves generation evaluation is unnecessary.

questions.question: Can a user retrieve a restricted policy just because it is indexed?
questions.answer: No. Enforce document access using the user’s identity before restricted content reaches the model or response.
questions.distractor: Yes, indexing makes all documents public.
